text:
alex: Heads-up — ran into inconsistent exception behavior in the Python SDK while onboarding a FastAPI sample. Sometimes a 422 returns ValidationError with .errors, other times APIError with raw bytes.
morgan: can you drop a tiny repro?
alex: yep, async snippet:```py
from redwood import RedwoodClient, ValidationError
client = RedwoodClient(api_key='x')
try:
    await client.chat.create(prompt='')
except ValidationError as e:
    print('structured:', e.errors)
except Exception as e:
    print('fallback:', type(e), getattr(e,'raw_body', None))
```
alex: Observed: `fallback <class 'redwood.errors.APIError'> b\"{\"detail\": \"required\"}\"` — raw bytes, no parsed_body.
rachel: that sounds familiar. We had a refactor where async transport didn't call the error JSON parser on non-application/json content-types and sometimes aiohttp returned bytes.
morgan: oi. Two fixes are needed: 1) canonicalize parsing — always try json.loads on the body inside a try/except, 2) normalize shapes: map common keys ("detail", "errors") -> ValidationError.errors as List[Dict[str,str]], 3) export concrete exceptions in typeshed so callers can `except ValidationError` and mypy picks it up.
docs-bot: Please add a quickstart snippet showing both sync+async try/except for ValidationError and AuthError, and demonstrate e.parsed_body vs e.raw_body. New users keep assuming a plain string.
alex: small API ask: include attributes on APIError: status_code (int), raw_body (bytes), parsed_body (optional[dict]), and for ValidationError add errors: List[Dict[str,str]]. Also keep APIError as base so existing except APIError continues to work.
morgan: add helper method APIError.is_retryable() -> bool (default True for 5xx and False for 4xx) to simplify backoff decisions.
rachel: types work: update errors.pyi and __init__.py to export APIError, AuthError, ValidationError. Add unit tests: runtime test that 401 raises AuthError, 422 raises ValidationError with .errors populated (both sync and async). Add mypy CI job to ensure consumers can import these names.
ci-bot: Created issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-python/issues/820 (py-sdk: normalize error parsing, export exceptions in typeshed)
morgan: also make sure ValidationError.errors is consistently a list of dicts even if upstream only provides a string. For example normalize {"detail": "x"} -> [{"message": "x"}].
alex: tiny DX note: include migration line in changelog: "Exceptions: ValidationError now consistent and exported; new attributes .errors, .raw_body, .parsed_body; AuthError export added."
ci-bot: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-python/pull/712 (normalize error parsing; export exceptions in types and add async tests)
rachel: PR LGTM pending green tests. I'll add the docs snippet after merge.
alex: verified locally on sample FastAPI app — both sync and async flows now raise ValidationError with structured .errors. thanks team :thumbsup:
morgan: assigned to @rachel for docs and @morgan for runtime/types. ETA: end of sprint.
